name: Trails at Pagosa Springs (now marketed as Timberline at Pagosa Springs)
headline: Generation Housing Partners, a Texas-based minority-owned developer, built a 50-unit family apartment complex for households at 30% to 80% AMI at 116 Alpha Drive near Walmart in uptown Pagosa Springs, with a $1,450,000-a-year 2023 Round One 9% award from CHFA; renamed Timberline, it was near completion in November 2025 and is now marketed for lease.
why_it_matters: It shows what a rural resort-county 9% deal needed to close after cost increases: a second-try credit award, a $4.75 million Division of Housing Transformational Housing Fund loan, extra CHFA loans, a $1.4 million deferred fee, town fee waivers and a contested partial water and sewer fee waiver tied to the developer repairing the district's sewer lines.

status.label: Built (near completion November 2025); leasing marketed; occupancy not public
status.detail: A Pagosa Daily Post photo dated November 2025 shows the Timberline apartments nearing completion, and an August 2026 Daily Post editorial says Generation Housing Partners constructed the 50-unit project; the property's website markets the homes and has a resident portal. In March 2025 the developer told the water district the site was not yet using water. No dated certificate of occupancy, placed-in-service date or occupancy figure was found.

next_step: Watch for CHFA's placed-in-service record and any town or Archuleta County Housing Authority record of occupancy or the property tax abatement.

background.text: The project applied in 2022 and won on its second application in 2023; the 2023 narrative added 70% and 80% AMI units using income averaging and noted that no existing Pagosa income-restricted project served those levels.

The planning commission approved the sketch design and the sketch subdivision of the master tract on 2024-02-13, and approved the final major design review unanimously on 2024-05-14, with conditions on stormwater, equipment screening and filing a final road design before a building permit. Neighbors in the Aspen Village subdivision raised traffic concerns about access through the Aspen Village Drive signal on US 160.

PAWSD's capital investment fee had risen from about $6,530 to about $24,700 per unit, so a 50-unit project faced close to $1 million. A motion for a full waiver failed 2-3 on 2024-05-23; the board then approved a partial waiver 4-0 with one abstention and paused further waivers until after the 2025 board election. The Daily Post editorials on this were written by its editor, who sat on the PAWSD board.

On 2024-07-25 PAWSD unanimously approved a main line extension acceptance agreement and a development agreement under which the developer repairs sewer inflow and infiltration problems downstream of the site; the minutes call the project 'Timberline (Trails at Pagosa Springs)'.

In March 2025 the developer asked PAWSD to bill the complex as one commercial account, saying it was charged for 51 equivalent units (about $4,000 a month in base rates) though designed to use about nine; the board formed a subcommittee. The developer said the waiver had only brought fees back down to about $300,000 after they rose to about $1.2 million during planning.
Soils on the site include fat clay over weathered and formational shale; the budget carried imported fill and extra equipment for cutting utilities in shale.
